title: Genitive: Taigh an sgùdair
question: What does 'taigh an sgùdair' mean?
explanation: In the genitive case, 'sgùdair' becomes 'sgùdair' (the possessor comes after 'an').

title: Genitive: Bean an fhear
question: What does 'bean an fhear' mean?
explanation: After 'an', masculine nouns lenite: 'an fhear' (the man).

title: Possessive vs Genitive
question: What is the difference? 'Mo bhràthair' vs 'bràthair an fhear'
correct: First is my brother, second is the man's brother
wrong2: First is possessive, second is possessive
wrong3: First is genitive, second is possessive
explanation: 'Mo bhràthair' (possessive) means 'my brother'; 'bràthair an fhear' (genitive) means 'the man's brother'.

title: Dative: Ann an Glaschu
question: What does 'ann an Glaschu' mean?
explanation: 'Ann an' + place name indicates location: 'ann an Glaschu' = 'in Glasgow'.

title: Dative: Ri an taigh
question: What does 'ri an taigh' mean?
explanation: 'Ri' can mean 'at' or 'by': 'ri an taigh' = 'by the house'.

title: Accusative: Chual mi an cù
question: What does 'chual mi an cù' mean?
explanation: 'Chual mi' (past tense of 'cluich'—listen/hear) with accusative object.

title: Lenition in past: Bhuail
question: What is the lenited form of 'buail' (hit) in past?
explanation: Verb roots lenite in the past tense: 'bhuail mi' = 'I hit'.

title: Lenition in future: Bhualaidh
question: What is the lenited form of 'buail' (hit) in future?
explanation: Regular future tense is 'ghabhaidh' forms, but 'buaidh' stays: 'bhuailidh'.

title: Conditional lenition: Bhuailidh
question: What form is 'bhuailidh'?
explanation: The conditional form of 'buail' is 'bhuailidh' — would hit.

title: Imperative singular: Buail!
question: What does 'Buail!' mean?
explanation: The imperative singular is the bare verbal root: 'Buail!' = 'Hit!'

title: Imperative plural: Buailidh
question: What does 'Buailidh sibh!' mean?
explanation: The future can function as a polite command: 'Buailidh sibh!' = 'Will you hit?'

title: Aspect: Simple past vs continuous
question: What is the difference between 'Dh'ith mi' and 'Bha mi ag ithe'?
correct: First is completed action, second is ongoing
wrong2: First is future, second is past
explanation: 'Dh'ith mi' (I ate) is perfective; 'bha mi ag ithe' (I was eating) is imperfective.

title: Reported speech: Thuirt
question: What does 'Thuirt mi...' mean?
explanation: 'Thuirt mi' is the past form of 'thuirt' (say) — 'I said'.

title: Reported speech: Gun
question: What does 'gun' indicate before a verb in reported speech?
explanation: 'Gun' introduces the complement in reported speech: 'Thuirt mi gun robh...' = 'I said that...'

title: Reported speech: Gu
question: What does 'gu' indicate in reported speech?
explanation: After 'tha', 'gu' introduces the complement: 'Tha mi creidsinn gu...' = 'I believe that...'

title: Nominalization: An t-ithe
question: What does 'an t-ithe' mean?
explanation: Verbal nouns can be nominalized with the article: 'an t-ithe' = 'the eating'.

title: Comparative: Nas motha
question: What does 'nas motha' mean?
explanation: 'Nas' creates the comparative: 'nas motha' = 'bigger'.

title: Superlative: As motha
question: What does 'as motha' mean?
explanation: 'As' creates the superlative: 'as motha' = 'biggest'.

title: Comparative: Fearr
question: What does 'fearr' mean?
explanation: 'Fearr' is the comparative of 'math' (good).

title: Superlative: As fearr
question: What does 'as fearr' mean?
explanation: 'As fearr' is the superlative of 'fearr'.

title: Negation: Nach eil mi
question: How do you say 'I am not' as a negative question?
explanation: 'Nach eil mi?' combines negation + interrogative: 'Am I not?'

title: Negation: Gu dearbh
question: What does 'gu dearbh' mean?
explanation: 'Gu dearbh' emphasizes affirmation: 'Tha, gu dearbh' = 'Yes, indeed'.

title: Emphasis: Is mise
question: What does the emphasis with 'is' do?
explanation: 'Is mise...' emphasizes the subject: 'Is mise Alasdair' = 'It is I who am Alexander'.

title: Relative past: A bha thu?
question: What does 'an duine a bha ann' mean?
explanation: 'A bha' is the past relative form: 'an duine a bha ann' = 'the man who was there'.

title: Relative future: A bhios tu?
question: What does 'an duine a bhios ann' mean?
correct: The man who will be there
explanation: 'A bhios' is the future relative: 'an duine a bhios ann' = 'the man who will be there'.

title: Conditional purpose: Gus an
question: What does 'gus an' mean?
explanation: 'Gus an' introduces a purpose or result clause: 'gus an robh mi sgìth' = 'until I was tired'.

title: Temporal: Nuair a
question: What does 'nuair a' mean?
explanation: 'Nuair a' introduces a temporal clause: 'nuair a thàinig e' = 'when he came'.

title: Conditional: Nan robh
question: What does 'nan robh mi ann' mean?
correct: If I were there (contrary to fact)
explanation: 'Nan robh' is the conditional ('if'), expressing contrary-to-fact scenarios.

title: Causative: Thug
question: What does 'thug mi dha leabhar' mean?
explanation: 'Thug' (gave) is the past of 'tabhann' (give) — direct object + indirect object word order.

title: Applicative: Chur
question: What does 'chur mi an leabhar air a' bhòrd' mean?
correct: I put the book on the table
wrong1: I took the book from the table
wrong2: I gave the book to the table
wrong3: I saw the book on the table
explanation: 'Chur' (put/place) uses dative object: 'air' (on).

title: Plural agreement: Na taighean boidheach
question: Is 'boidheach' lenited after plural?
correct: No — only singular feminine nouns trigger lenition
explanation: In plural, adjectives don't lenite: 'na taighean boidheach' = 'the beautiful houses'.

title: Consonant lenition rule
question: Which consonants lenite in Gaelic?
correct: B, C, D, F, G, M, P, S, T
explanation: Lenition affects: B→bh, C→ch, D→dh, F→fh, G→gh, M→mh, P→ph, S→sh, T→th.

title: Lenition context: After 'an t-'
question: Does 'an t-' trigger lenition of the following vowel word?
correct: No — it only protects vowels with 't-'
explanation: 'An t-' prefixes 't-' to vowels for pronunciation ease; no lenition.

title: Prepositional + article fusion
question: What does 'den' mean?
explanation: 'Den' is the fusion of 'de' (from) + 'an' (the): 'den taigh' = 'from the house'.
